name: Light Coral Red
lede: Light Coral Red is a vivid salmon-pink from Ridgway's 1912 atlas, filed again by name in the 1955 ISCC-NBS dictionary, close on screen to both Bittersweet and Salmon.

sections.title: A Ridgway tone, vivid and warm
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* carries this swatch on plate XIII, hue 5′, tone b [1]. The 1955 ISCC-NBS dictionary files the exact name "Light Coral Red" under block 35, "strong reddish orange" [2]. The name builds "light" onto [[coral-red]], after the pink-to-red tones found in reef coral [1].

In our color library its closest neighbors are [[bittersweet]] and [[salmon]], both about 3.1 units away, close enough to pass for the same color [3]. [[terracotta]] sits 3.4 units off, also nearly indistinguishable, and Bright Terracotta 3.6 units off, more vivid [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive of 23,781 paintings matches this tone in 27 of them, about 0.11 percent, as photographed, rarer than 60 percent of the named colors we track [4]. It peaks in the 1500s, present in 5 of the 2,231 paintings from that century, 2.0 times the rate its museums' own baseline would predict [4].

Inside a painting it most often plays an accent, in 71 percent of its 21 clearly-ranked appearances [4]. The earliest dated match is 1236, 676 years before the name's first 1912 record, so this is a look-alike hue in an old photograph, not proof of the name's age [4]. The archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, and the match is a computed color reading, not a pigment identification [4].

origin.named_after: the modifier "light" plus [[coral-red]], after reef coral
